STRUCTURAL from the decomp (the seed, the roll, one Random() per VBlank); the frame counts of the presses after naming are emulator-measured on mGBA 0.10.5 by two independent harnesses, both committed in this repository (tools/gba-sid-harness with agbcc-built symbol addresses; tools/gen3-sid-savestate-harness with a savestate binary search), byte-exact ROM, text speeds fast / mid / slow, name lengths 1, 4 and 7: k_fixed 680 / 1645 / 2937 with a 1-letter name, 692 / 1693 / 3033 with 7 letters. Not yet checked on hardware (whole-VBlank counters in the game code, expected to transfer exactly, unlike Gen 1's DIV-stirred bytes).
emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1.predicts: the Secret ID (and TSV) from a typed Trainer ID: one candidate per k; a narrow k window with the press cue; one candidate with a pin
emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1.protocol: Play to the player naming screen and enter the name. The A on OK is the anchor: the game fades out, reads Timer1 24 frames later, stores that count as the Trainer ID and seeds the RNG with it. From there the RNG advances once per VBlank until CB2_NewGame rolls the Secret ID; that span holds 9 timed presses (k_fixed 680 fast / 1645 mid / 2937 slow with a 1-letter name) (YES on 'So it's X?' and the 8 text waits of Birch's two closing texts: 6 paragraph ends and 2 scroll prompts), each a JOY_NEW read, so k = the fixed frame counts + the lateness of each press. Every press after naming: tap A once when the box is ready (the arrow, the YES/NO box), never press before the box is ready (the press is swallowed, and it arms the hold-to-speed-up); a held A on a waiting box is harmless, a held A after a press during printing is not. Read the Trainer ID off the Trainer Card and type it; the tool lists the Secret ID per k. With --cue the presses are beeped at known times, so k is a window of a few frames; a later pin (a PID you can see is shiny or not) narrows the list to one.
validity: Pokemon Emerald (English) on GBA silicon or a GBA emulator: the counts are VBlank counters in the game code, not console timing.
A New Game whose player name went through the naming screen (always the case) and whose 'So it's X?' box was answered YES the FIRST time: a NO re-rolls the Trainer ID and re-enters this span.

The OPTIONS text speed is stated to the tool (no default: the PSR Emerald route sets FAST from the main menu's OPTION entry before NEW GAME, a fresh cartridge is MID); fast, mid and slow are all measured.

Every press after naming is one tap of A on a box that is already waiting (the arrow or the YES/NO box). Never press while the text is still printing: that press is swallowed AND arms the hold-to-speed-up (text.c:944-955 / :639-650: a held A then prints one character per frame), after which a held A changes the counts. A plain held A on a waiting box is harmless (measured: A held 8 or 30 frames at every press gives the same k as one-frame taps). B is never used: B on the name box answers NO and re-rolls the Trainer ID, and B is also accepted by the text waits (not measured).
The player name length is stated to the tool (it changes the printing time of the two boxes that show the name).
The Trainer ID typed is the one on the Trainer Card of that save; a pin (shiny / not shiny PID) is a fact about that save only.
Any other input pattern (a held A, a press while the text is still printing, an OPTIONS change, a link or a battle before the roll) gives a different k that this model does not cover.
emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1.table: no table: SID = high 16 bits of LCRNG^(k+1)(TID), x = 0x41C64E6D*x + 0x6073 mod 2^32; k = 680 (fast) / 1645 (mid) / 2937 (slow) fixed VBlanks with a 1-letter name (692 / 1693 / 3033 with 7 letters) + the presses' lateness; the fixed part is the 'model' block
emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1.derivation: decomp trace (citations below) for the mechanism; mGBA 0.10.5 headless (RetroBridge mgx shim, byte-exact ROM) for the counts: the seed instant is the frame TM1CNT_H drops to 0 and gRngValue holds the 16-bit Trainer ID, the roll is the frame SaveBlock2.playerTrainerId is written, and each press is scripted on the first frame its box accepts input (the game's task or printer state, read from memory), held two frames and read back from gMain.newKeys (a main-loop iteration that overruns a frame has no pad read: LeafGreen's rival menu shows one). The observed SID equals hi16(LCRNG^(k+1)(TID)) at the frame-counted k in every run; the all-earliest SIDs are also inverted from k = 0 in tests/test_gen3.py
emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1.validation: emulator-measured only. Slope test: every press d frames late moves k by exactly d x the press count (d = 0 / 10 / 60 on every path and speed; tools/gba-sid-harness/RESULTS.md). The all-earliest run's SID is the LCRNG's high 16 bits at k+1 from the seed in every run, and the LCRNG advanced exactly once per frame of the span and twice on the roll frame (no other Random() on the path). Two harnesses, two address sources, two press protocols, both committed in this repository: the tools/gen3-sid-savestate-harness binary search and tools/gba-sid-harness agree to the frame on every row both measured. No hardware sample yet.

rs/gba/boot-seed-v0.protocol: The RNG is seeded once at boot from the RTC minute count (a dead battery gives the dummy RTC, 2000-01-01 day 1, minute count 1440 = 0x5A0: the same seed every boot). Nothing on the New Game path reseeds, and the name confirm does not touch the ID. The Trainer ID and Secret ID are two consecutive Random() calls in InitPlayerTrainerId, reached through CB2_NewGame after the FINAL Birch box; the last A on Birch is the timed press, counted in frames from the boot (or from the fixed dead-battery seed).
validity: Ruby or Sapphire on GBA silicon, with the RTC battery state known: alive (seed = minute count at boot) or dead (seed 0x5A0 every boot).
No reseed between the boot and the ID roll; the number of Random() calls before InitPlayerTrainerId is fixed by the input path taken (STRUCTURAL claim; the sequence is not tabulated yet).
The timed press is the final A on the Birch speech; entering or changing the name does not change the ID.

e-frlg/gba/naming-exit-v0.name: Timer1 read at the player-naming-screen exit sets the Trainer ID; the Secret ID follows from that seed
e-frlg/gba/naming-exit-v0.status: DEFINED ONLY, and SUPERSEDED 2026-09-02 by emerald/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1, firered/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1 and leafgreen/gba/typed-tid-sid-v1 (the sid subcommand), whose fixed frame counts are emulator-measured on mGBA 0.10.5 by two independent harnesses, both committed in this repository (tools/gba-sid-harness, tools/gen3-sid-savestate-harness) with byte-exact ROMs: Emerald k_fixed 680 (fast) / 1645 (mid) / 2937 (slow) with a 1-letter name and 9 presses; FireRed 1868 (NEW NAME rival 'A', 11 presses) / 1781 (preset rival, 8 timed presses plus an untimed DOWN) at MID, LeafGreen 1868 / 1765; slopes exactly one frame of k per frame of lateness on every press. Kept for the record: its 'six paragraph waits' were an INFERRED count; the trace and the measurement give YES + 8 text waits in Emerald (6 paragraph ends and 2 scroll prompts).
e-frlg/gba/naming-exit-v0.predicts: the Secret ID from a typed Trainer ID (the Trainer ID itself is a sub-frame Timer1 count)
e-frlg/gba/naming-exit-v0.protocol: Timer1 starts when the player-naming screen is set up and is read at that screen's exit (after OK and the fade): the 16-bit count becomes the Trainer ID and seeds the RNG, and the Secret ID is then Random() << 16 in InitPlayerTrainerId. Timer1 counts 16.78 MHz cycles, so the Trainer ID is a sub-frame quantity nobody can choose by hand; what a runner can do is enter the Trainer ID they got, from which the Secret ID follows. Between the seed and the SID roll the RNG advances once per VBlank, and that span runs from the naming-screen exit to CB2_NewGame: through the 'So it's X?' box and its YES press and through Birch's closing text with its six paragraph waits, each a press. So the Secret ID depends on the press timing AFTER naming (STRUCTURAL), like the final Birch box in Ruby / Sapphire, and a cue for those presses can pin it; the fixed frame counts of the fades and text printers in that span are not yet measured (INFERRED). FireRed / LeafGreen also set the ID once at the title-screen exit, but the naming-screen exit always overwrites it on a New Game.
validity: Emerald, FireRed or LeafGreen on GBA silicon.
A New Game whose player name went through the naming screen (always: FireRed / LeafGreen's preset-name menu is rival-only).
The Trainer ID is read off the trainer card, not chosen; NO on the 'So it's X?' box goes back through naming and rerolls it.

The Secret ID prediction needs k, the number of frames from the naming-screen exit to the final white fade before the overworld (the YES press and the six paragraph presses of Birch's closing text lie inside it): one candidate per k, or one candidate when those presses are cued.
e-frlg/gba/naming-exit-v0.target_mode: not achievable by timing: enter the Trainer ID you got and the tool will predict the Secret ID (planned: one candidate per post-naming frame count k, pinned by cueing the presses after naming).
